- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often underestimates or overshoots mid-range; apply mean reversion to 10–15 day moving average.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast increase to +3% max from prior peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates by 1–4% in early forecast days; apply linear decay correction: subtract 0.1–0.3% per day from forecast starting day 5.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.33/1.00 alternation, model exhibits oscillation bias; smooth forecast with 3-day weighted average to dampen noise.
